name: BanglaTrace
description: This dataset is a cross-stage benchmark for the front end of Bangla text-to-speech. It follows the outputs of text normalization (TN) through grapheme-to-phoneme (G2P) conversion and speech synthesis, so that errors can be located and measured at each stage. It contains 485 author-written Bangla sentences in 40 categories (numbers, dates and times, money and measurements, acronyms, code-mixed and romanized text, identifiers, and plain-text controls) across 12 application domains. The sentences have 548 annotated non-standard-word spans and 2,181 accepted sentence readings at three levels (PRIMARY, STRICT, FULL), and are split into 93 development and 392 test sentences. The record also includes: saved outputs of six TN conditions: raw text, bnNumerizer, NumericContext, PyBangla, Google's public WFST grammars, and an adapted Kingfisher with GPT-OSS 120B; TN-to-G2P interface results for Epitran and eSpeak NG; speech results for two synthesizers with different input representations, the character-input MMS-TTS and the subword-input Indic Parler-TTS, each recognized by MMS-ASR and Whisper large-v3; error-source and failure-type analyses; G2P agreement with the Google Bengali pronunciation lexicon; the systematic-review appraisal records; the code that regenerates every table and figure. It accompanies the article "Tracing Errors from Text to Speech: A Systematic Review and Cross-Stage Benchmark of Bangla Text Normalization and Pronunciation" (submitted to ACM TALLIP).
